checklist.step: Freeze the valuation date and issue the run timetable
actions: Publish the quarter's valuation timetable: data-extract date, assumption-lock date, model-run window, review dates and the Appointed Actuary sign-off date, backed off working day 10.
Circulate the timetable to the Reserving Analysts, Data Engineering and Finance close owners and confirm receipt.
Confirm with the Statutory Reporting Manager that the annual cycle lands ahead of the BMA Statutory Financial Return date (four months after year end).
Log the timetable in the close calendar with T-20/T-10/T-5 alerts.
checklist.done: a dated timetable exists in the close calendar with every owner named and alerts armed.

checklist.step: Extract the policy inforce file from the policy administration system
actions: Run the valuation extract job against the Policy Administration Platform as at the frozen valuation date, pulling policy number, plan code, issue date, status, face amount, account value, premiums and rider indicators.
Land the extract in the enterprise data warehouse valuation schema with a run id and row count.
Hand the Reserving Analyst the control totals: policy count, sum assured and account value by product line.
Retain the extract job log with the run id in the valuation folder.
checklist.done: the inforce extract is landed with a run id and control totals delivered to the Reserving Analyst.

checklist.step: Reconcile the extract to admin-system control totals and prior quarter
actions: Compare extract policy counts and amounts to the Policy Administration Platform's own period-end control report, by product line.
Roll forward from prior quarter: opening count + new business − terminations = closing count; chase any residual over 0.5% with Policy Administration.
Document every difference with cause (late-processed claims, backdated issues) on the data reconciliation tab.
Get the Data Quality Analyst to countersign the reconciliation before model load.
checklist.done: counts and amounts reconcile within 0.5% with all differences explained and countersigned.

checklist.step: Update and lock the valuation assumptions per the approved basis
actions: Pull the current approved assumption basis (mortality, lapse, expense, discount/EBS risk-free curve) from the model governance repository.
Load the BMA-published EBS risk-free discount curves for the valuation date and file the source download.
List any proposed assumption change with rationale and reserve impact estimate on an assumption memo.
Lock the assumption set at the assumption-lock date — later changes require Chief Actuary approval in writing.
checklist.done: the assumption set is locked, sourced, and any change is documented on a memo awaiting approval.

checklist.step: Approve assumption changes through the assumptions committee
actions: Table each assumption memo at the assumptions committee with the experience-study evidence behind it.
Approve, reject or defer each change and minute the decision with names and date.
Ensure any material basis change is flagged for disclosure in the valuation report and, where material to solvency, assessed for BMA notification.
Return the approved basis to the Valuation Actuary and update the model governance repository.
checklist.done: every assumption change carries a minuted committee decision and the repository holds the approved basis.

checklist.step: Build and load the model point files
actions: Transform the reconciled extract into model point files per the documented grouping rules (no grouping for material blocks, per the Reserving Policy).
Load the model point files into FIS Prophet and record the file names, row counts and checksums in the run log.
Reconcile model point counts and sums back to the extract control totals; investigate any drop-outs.
File the load log in the valuation folder.
checklist.done: model points are loaded with counts and sums tied back to the extract and a saved load log.

checklist.step: Run the best-estimate liability projections
actions: Execute the locked-basis best-estimate run for each product line in the actuarial modeling platform, using the versioned model release recorded in the model governance repository.
Capture run ids, model version, assumption set id and runtime warnings into the run log.
Spot-check seriatim results for five known policies per line against hand calculations.
Export the best-estimate liability by product line to the results workbook.
checklist.done: best-estimate runs complete on the locked basis with run ids logged and seriatim spot-checks passed.

checklist.step: Compute the EBS risk margin
actions: Compute the risk margin per the BMA EBS rules (cost-of-capital approach on projected capital for non-hedgeable risks) using the current BSCR parameters.
Document the projection of capital requirements and the cost-of-capital rate applied, with the BMA source for each parameter.
Reconcile the risk margin movement against prior quarter and explain drivers.
Hand the risk margin schedule to the Valuation Actuary for inclusion in technical provisions.
checklist.done: the risk margin is computed on current BMA parameters with a documented, reconciled schedule.

checklist.step: Produce the statutory basis alongside the EBS basis
actions: Run or derive the statutory-basis reserves required for the Statutory Financial Statements in parallel with EBS technical provisions.
Tabulate both bases by product line in the results workbook with a bridge explaining basis differences.
Confirm the aggregate technical provisions equal best-estimate liability plus risk margin on the EBS view.
Flag any negative reserves or floor breaches for the Appointed Actuary's attention.
checklist.done: both bases are tabulated with a documented bridge and flags on any floor issues.

checklist.step: Perform the movement analysis
actions: Roll reserves forward from prior quarter: expected change (unwind, premiums, claims), new business, assumption changes, model changes and experience variance.
Attribute each movement component by product line and compare against the pre-set 1%-of-opening-reserves unexplained tolerance.
Investigate any unexplained residual over tolerance down to model point level before sign-off.
Write the movement commentary into the valuation report draft.
checklist.done: the movement analysis explains the quarter's change within tolerance with written commentary.

checklist.step: Peer review the runs and results
actions: Have an actuary who did not execute the runs re-check: assumption set id versus the approved basis, model version versus the governance repository, and results-workbook formulas.
Re-perform the seriatim spot-checks independently for two policies per line.
Record review points and their resolution on the peer-review checklist.
Sign and date the peer-review checklist.
checklist.done: a signed peer-review checklist exists with every review point closed.

checklist.step: Compile the valuation workpaper pack
actions: Assemble into one indexed pack: extract logs, reconciliations, assumption memos and approvals, run logs, risk margin schedule, movement analysis, peer-review checklist and the results workbook.
Name the pack REG-054-C01-<yyyyQx> and file it in the financial reporting repository with the 10-year retention label.
Cross-reference each pack section to the Reserving Policy control it evidences.
Confirm the pack index has no empty sections.
checklist.done: an indexed, retention-labelled workpaper pack is filed with no gaps.

checklist.step: Obtain Appointed Actuary review and sign-off
actions: Review the workpaper pack, challenge the movement drivers and assumption changes, and confirm the technical provisions comply with the BMA EBS rules and the Reserving Policy.
Document challenges raised and their resolution in the sign-off memo.
Sign the valuation summary, dating the sign-off inside the timetable window.
Release the signed reserves to Finance for ledger posting.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary's dated sign-off memo and signed valuation summary are in the pack.

checklist.step: Post the reserve balances to the general ledger
actions: Post the signed reserve balances by product line to the reserve accounts in SAP S/4HANA (GL) using the standard valuation journal template.
Attach the signed valuation summary to the journal entry as support.
Reconcile posted balances to the results workbook to the dollar and resolve any difference before close.
Notify the Statutory Reporting Manager that reserves are final for the statutory returns.
checklist.done: GL reserve balances equal the signed valuation summary and Statutory Reporting is notified.

checklist.step: Log exceptions and assess BMA self-reporting
actions: Log every valuation exception (unapproved assumption change, reconciliation break above tolerance, late sign-off) in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with root cause and owner.
Assess with the Appointed Actuary whether any exception is a material failure to comply with the Insurance Code of Conduct requiring self-report to the BMA.
Where self-report is warranted, draft the notification with remediation plan and route it through the General Counsel before sending.
Track remediation to closure with Chief Actuary sign-off.
checklist.done: every exception is logged with disposition and any material Code breach has a documented self-report decision.

testing.step: Build the population of reserve balances for the period
actions: Pull the signed valuation summaries for each quarter under test from the financial reporting repository.
List every product line / valuation basis cell with its reserve balance as the test population.
Confirm no product line present in the policy admin extract is missing from the valuation summary.
testing.done: a complete cell-level population is listed and tied to the signed valuation summaries.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the general ledger
actions: Agree each quarter's total reserves per the valuation summary to the reserve account balances in SAP S/4HANA (GL).
Trace the posting journal and confirm the signed summary was attached as support.
List any dollar difference as an automatic exception.
testing.done: valuation summaries agree to the GL to the dollar or differences are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of valuation cells
actions: Select the three largest product-line cells per quarter plus five random cells drawn with a recorded seed.
Include at least one cell with an assumption change and one with a model change in the period.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is documented covering large, changed and random cells.

testing.step: Re-perform a model run for sampled cells
actions: Re-run the sampled cells in the actuarial modeling platform using the archived model version, model points and locked assumption set from the run log.
Compare re-run results to the reported reserves; any difference beyond rounding is an exception.
Capture re-run ids and outputs into the test workpaper.
testing.done: re-runs reproduce reported reserves within rounding for every sampled cell.

testing.step: Verify assumptions trace to the approved basis
actions: For each sampled cell, agree the assumption set id in the run log to the approved basis in the model governance repository.
For any assumption changed in the period, verify a minuted assumptions-committee approval dated before the run date.
Treat any assumption without an approval trail as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled assumption traces to an approved, pre-dated basis.

testing.step: Recompute the risk margin arithmetic
actions: Recompute the cost-of-capital risk margin from the capital projection schedule using the BMA-published parameters for the valuation date.
Agree the parameters used to the BMA source documents filed in the pack.
Compare to the reported risk margin and log any difference over 0.1% as an exception.
testing.done: the recomputed risk margin matches the reported figure on verified BMA parameters.

testing.step: Trace source data through the reconciliation chain
actions: For two sampled cells, trace control totals from the Policy Administration Platform period-end report through the warehouse extract to the model point load log.
Verify the data reconciliation was countersigned by the Data Quality Analyst before model load.
Confirm residual differences were within the 0.5% tolerance and explained.
testing.done: the data chain is traced end-to-end with countersigned reconciliations inside tolerance.

testing.step: Verify movement analysis and sign-off timing
actions: Check each quarter's movement analysis explains the reserve change with unexplained residual under 1% of opening reserves.
Verify the Appointed Actuary sign-off date fell inside the timetable and, for year end, ahead of the BMA Statutory Financial Return date.
Verify the peer-review checklist was signed by a non-performer before sign-off.
testing.done: movement residuals are within tolerance and sign-offs are dated, sequenced and independent.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the cell, quarter, control missed and impact on the reported reserves.
Assign root cause (data, assumption governance, model version, timing) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Flag any exception that indicates a material Code breach to the Compliance Officer for BMA self-report assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retest cells.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-unapproved-change and reconciliation thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — who performed no sampled valuation work — sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C01.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Open the annual opinion file and confirm scope
actions: Open the opinion file for the fiscal year and list every liability block in scope: reserves by product line, both statutory and EBS bases, and any ceded/assumed reinsurance balances relied on.
Confirm scope covers 100% of the entity's insurance liabilities by agreeing the block list to the signed valuation summary.
Confirm the signature deadline: 15 working days before the BMA Statutory Financial Return date (four months after year end).
Record scope and deadline in the opinion file index.
checklist.done: the opinion file lists every liability block, ties to the valuation summary and carries the signature deadline.

checklist.step: Collect reliance data and written representations
actions: Request from the Controller a written representation that the ledger balances supplied to the valuation are complete and accurate.
Request from the Data Quality Analyst the year-end data reconciliation pack with its countersignature.
Request from the Reinsurance Accountant the ceded balances and treaty listing relied on in the reserves.
File each reliance letter, dated and signed, in the opinion file.
checklist.done: signed reliance letters from Finance, Data and Reinsurance are on file for every relied-upon input.

checklist.step: Verify the valuation conformed to the approved reserving policy
actions: Walk the year-end valuation pack against the Reserving Policy clause by clause: methods, assumption governance, data controls, run controls and sign-off chain.
List any departure from policy with its rationale and materiality on a conformity memo.
Confirm every assumption change carried a minuted assumptions-committee approval.
Hand the conformity memo to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: a conformity memo confirms policy adherence with every departure listed and assessed.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial opinion
actions: Draft the opinion in the document management repository using the procedure's template: identification of the actuary and appointment, scope of liabilities, standards applied (BMA EBS rules and the entity's Reserving Policy), reliance statements, and the opinion sentence on the adequacy of the liabilities.
State the opinion type plainly — unqualified, qualified, adverse or inconclusive — and the reasons for any qualification.
Quote the reserve amounts opined on to the dollar, agreeing them to the signed valuation summary.
Version the draft and restrict edit access to the actuarial function.
checklist.done: a versioned draft opinion states scope, standards, reliances and an explicit opinion on stated amounts.

checklist.step: Prepare the supporting actuarial memorandum
actions: Write the memorandum to the procedure's content list: data description and reconciliation results, methods by product line, assumption table with change history, risk margin derivation, movement analysis, sensitivity results and areas of judgement.
Cross-reference each memorandum section to the valuation workpaper pack (REG-054-C01) so every figure is traceable.
Include the conformity memo findings and how departures were resolved.
File the memorandum alongside the draft opinion.
checklist.done: the memorandum covers the full content list with cross-references into the valuation workpapers.

checklist.step: Run sensitivity and adverse-scenario support for the opinion
actions: Run the procedure's standard sensitivity set in the actuarial modeling platform: mortality +/-10%, lapse +/-20%, expense +10%, and a 100bp discount-curve shift.
Tabulate the reserve impact of each sensitivity by product line into the memorandum's sensitivity section.
Flag to the Appointed Actuary any sensitivity that would exhaust the margin in the held reserves.
Archive the sensitivity run ids alongside the base run log.
checklist.done: the standard sensitivity set is run, tabulated in the memorandum and flagged where margins thin.

checklist.step: Obtain independent peer review of the opinion and memorandum
actions: Assign a reviewing actuary who performed none of the year-end valuation runs.
Review the draft opinion against the memorandum: amounts agree, reliances match the letters on file, opinion type is supported by the conformity memo and sensitivities.
Record review comments and their resolution on the peer-review log.
Sign and date the peer-review log before signature is scheduled.
checklist.done: an independent peer-review log is signed with all comments resolved.

checklist.step: Brief the Chief Actuary and resolve qualification questions
actions: Review the draft opinion, memorandum, conformity memo and sensitivity table with the Appointed Actuary.
Where a qualification is contemplated, agree the wording and the remediation expectation, and involve the General Counsel on regulatory consequences.
Minute the briefing outcome and any conditions attached to signature.
Confirm the signature date remains ahead of the internal 15-working-day buffer.
checklist.done: the briefing is minuted, qualification wording (if any) is settled, and the signature date holds.

checklist.step: Sign and date the opinion
actions: Execute the final opinion via DocuSign, applying signature and date, and lock the signed PDF against edit.
Verify the signed version equals the peer-reviewed version (compare document hash or version id).
Confirm the signature date precedes the BMA Statutory Financial Return filing date.
Store the signed opinion and final memorandum in the document management repository with the 10-year retention label.
checklist.done: a signed, dated, locked opinion matching the peer-reviewed version is archived with retention applied.

checklist.step: Deliver the signed opinion to Regulatory Reporting and the Board
actions: Hand the signed opinion to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for inclusion in the Statutory Financial Return package (filed under REG-054-C03).
Present the opinion and key memorandum findings to the Audit Committee at its pre-filing meeting.
Provide the Board with the sensitivity table and any qualification explanation for its minutes.
Record the delivery dates in the opinion file.
checklist.done: Regulatory Reporting holds the signed opinion and the Audit Committee presentation is minuted.

checklist.step: Track and close opinion-cycle exceptions
actions: Log in the regulatory filing/issue tracker any missed milestone, missing reliance letter, unresolved peer-review comment or qualification issued.
Assign each item a root cause, owner and remediation date.
Route material items to the Compliance Officer for BMA self-report assessment under the Code's consequences-of-non-compliance provisions.
Close items only on Chief Actuary sign-off.
checklist.done: every cycle exception is logged, owned, assessed for reportability and closed with sign-off.

checklist.step: Maintain the Appointed Actuary's appointment evidence
actions: Confirm the Board resolution appointing the Appointed Actuary is current and filed in the board portal.
Verify the actuary's qualification and professional-body membership certificates are on file and unexpired.
Where the appointment changed in the year, confirm the BMA was notified of the change per the Insurance Act requirements.
File the appointment evidence reference in the opinion file.
checklist.done: current appointment resolution and qualification evidence are on file and referenced.

checklist.step: Update the reserving policy from opinion findings
actions: Review the memorandum's areas-of-judgement and conformity departures for changes the Reserving Policy needs.
Draft policy amendments and table them for Board re-approval at the next scheduled review.
Record in the model governance repository any model or assumption-governance changes committed to.
Link the amendment record back to the opinion file.
checklist.done: policy follow-ups from the opinion are drafted, tabled and traceable to the opinion file.

checklist.step: Archive the complete opinion file
actions: Assemble the final file: signed opinion, memorandum, reliance letters, conformity memo, sensitivity runs, peer-review log, briefing minutes and delivery records.
Index the file and store it in the document management repository under entity/year with the 10-year retention label.
Verify each index entry opens and the signed opinion PDF is the locked version.
Notify the Compliance Analyst the file is complete for the annual test.
checklist.done: a complete, indexed, retention-labelled opinion file is archived and flagged for testing.

checklist.step: Set next year's opinion timetable
actions: Back-schedule next year's milestones from the next SFR filing date: reliance-letter requests, draft date, peer review, Chief Actuary briefing and signature buffer.
Load the milestones into the close calendar with T-60/T-30/T-15 alerts.
Confirm owners for each milestone accept the dates.
File the timetable in the new opinion file.
checklist.done: next year's milestones are calendared with alerts and accepted owners.

testing.step: Build the population of opinions and supporting files
actions: List every actuarial opinion signed for the entity in the review period from the document management repository.
Reconcile the list to the fiscal years requiring an opinion — one per year, no gaps.
Pull each opinion's file index as the test inventory.
testing.done: one opinion per required year is confirmed with file indexes pulled.

testing.step: Reconcile opined amounts to the source of record
actions: Agree the reserve amounts stated in each opinion to the signed valuation summary and to the year-end reserve balances in SAP S/4HANA (GL).
Any mismatch between opinion, valuation summary and ledger is an automatic exception.
Record the tie-out in the workpaper with document references.
testing.done: opined amounts agree to valuation summary and ledger for every year, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Verify signature, dating and deadline compliance
actions: Check each opinion bears the Appointed Actuary's signature and a date preceding the BMA Statutory Financial Return filing date for that year.
Verify the signed PDF is locked and matches the peer-reviewed version by hash or version id.
Recompute the four-months-after-year-end filing deadline and confirm the signature preceded it.
testing.done: every opinion is signed, dated, version-verified and pre-dates the recomputed filing deadline.

testing.step: Re-perform the memorandum content check
actions: Walk the memorandum against the procedure's content list item by item: data reconciliation, methods, assumption change history, risk margin, movement, sensitivities, judgements.
Mark each item present/absent without reference to any prior checklist.
Any absent item is an exception.
testing.done: an independent content walk shows every required memorandum section present.

testing.step: Verify reliance letters exist and pre-date signature
actions: For each reliance stated in the opinion, locate the signed letter from Finance, Data or Reinsurance in the opinion file.
Check each letter's date precedes the opinion signature date.
A reliance stated without a letter, or a letter dated after signature, is a fail.
testing.done: every stated reliance is backed by a signed, pre-dated letter.

testing.step: Re-perform the conformity judgement on a sample basis
actions: Independently re-walk three Reserving Policy clauses (assumption governance, data controls, sign-off chain) against the year-end valuation pack without reading the conformity memo first.
Compare conclusions to the conformity memo; differences, including unlisted departures, are exceptions.
Document the re-performance notes in the workpaper.
testing.done: independent conformity re-performance matches the memo or differences are logged.

testing.step: Recompute sensitivity support for the opinion type
actions: Re-foot the sensitivity table and agree two sensitivities to the archived run outputs by run id.
Assess whether any sensitivity that exhausts reserve margins was flagged and reflected in the opinion type.
An unqualified opinion sitting on an unaddressed margin-exhausting sensitivity is an exception for escalation.
testing.done: sensitivity arithmetic verifies and the opinion type is consistent with flagged results.

testing.step: Verify peer review independence and resolution
actions: Confirm the peer reviewer named on the log performed none of the year-end valuation runs (check run logs for their id).
Verify every review comment shows a resolution and the log was signed before the opinion signature date.
Reviewer overlap with run execution is an independence exception.
testing.done: peer review was independent, fully resolved and pre-dated signature.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the year, requirement missed and impact on opinion reliability.
Assign root cause (timetable, reliance gap, content gap, independence) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Refer potential material Code breaches to the Compliance Officer for BMA self-report assessment.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: each exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and reportability referral.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off and Audit Committee reporting
actions: State the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) against the zero-tolerance threshold with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer sign the workpaper confirming segregation from the actuarial function.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee alongside the opinion presentation cycle.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C02.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Confirm the filing deadline and open the filing record
actions: Compute the filing deadline as four months after the fiscal year end (30 April for a 31 December year end) and verify it against the BMA's current filing instructions.
Open the year's filing record in the Internal Regulatory System with the deadline and T-60/T-30/T-10/T-3 reminders.
Record the BMA portal account, the authorised submitters and their access status.
Attach the BMA instruction pack for the filing year to the record.
checklist.done: the filing record carries the computed deadline, reminders, submitter access confirmation and the year's BMA instructions.

checklist.step: Download and apply the BMA's current-year filing instructions
actions: Download the current Statutory Financial Return and Capital and Solvency Return instructions and templates from the BMA website for the entity's licence class.
Diff the schedule list against last year's package and list every added, removed or changed schedule.
Circulate the change list to the Statutory Reporting Manager, Appointed Actuary and Capital Model Actuary with owners per schedule.
File the instruction download with its date in the filing record.
checklist.done: current instructions are on file and every schedule change has a named owner.

checklist.step: Assemble the statutory financial statements and SFR schedules
actions: Build the statutory financial statements and SFR schedules from the closed ledger, agreeing every reserve line to the signed valuation summary (REG-054-C01).
Complete the Economic Balance Sheet schedules with the technical provisions (best estimate plus risk margin) from the valuation pack.
Run the package checklist from the BMA Annual Filing Procedure and tick each required schedule.
Store the assembled package in the financial reporting repository with version control.
checklist.done: a version-controlled package matches the BMA checklist with reserves agreed to the signed valuation.

checklist.step: Attach the signed actuarial opinion to the package
actions: Retrieve the signed, locked opinion PDF from the document management repository (produced under REG-054-C02).
Verify the signature and date are present and the opined amounts equal the reserve lines in the SFR schedules to the dollar.
Insert the opinion into the package at the position the BMA instructions specify.
Record the opinion version id in the filing record.
checklist.done: the signed opinion is in the package, amount-matched to the schedules, with its version id logged.

checklist.step: Obtain officer certifications and declarations
actions: Route the statutory declarations to the required signatories (directors and officers per the BMA instructions) through DocuSign.
Track completion daily against the T-10 milestone and chase unsigned declarations.
Verify signatory names and titles match the current officer register.
File completed declarations into the package.
checklist.done: all required declarations are signed by verified officers and filed in the package.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission quality review
actions: Review the full package against the checklist: every schedule present, cross-schedule totals consistent, opinion attached, declarations signed.
Have the Appointed Actuary confirm in writing that the actuarial content (opinion and EBS schedules) is the final signed version.
Have the Controller confirm the financial statements tie to the closed ledger.
Sign the pre-submission review sheet and freeze the package version.
checklist.done: a signed review sheet confirms completeness and the package version is frozen.

checklist.step: Submit the package through the BMA electronic filing portal
actions: Log in to the BMA's electronic filing portal with the entity's authorised submitter credentials.
Open the annual filing task for the entity's licence class, upload each schedule and the signed opinion to its designated slot, and complete the portal's declaration fields.
Resolve any portal validation errors by correcting the source schedule — never by editing figures in the portal alone.
Submit before the deadline and download the portal's submission confirmation with its timestamp.
checklist.done: the portal shows a submitted status and a timestamped confirmation is downloaded.

checklist.step: File the submission confirmation and close the deadline milestone
actions: Attach the portal confirmation and the as-filed package to the filing record in the Internal Regulatory System.
Mark the deadline milestone met, recording submission date versus deadline date.
Store the as-filed package and confirmation in the financial reporting repository with the 10-year retention label.
Notify the CFO, Appointed Actuary and Compliance Officer that the filing is complete.
checklist.done: the filing record shows a met deadline with confirmation and the as-filed package archived.

checklist.step: Monitor for BMA acknowledgement or deficiency notices
actions: Check the BMA portal messages and the registered correspondence inbox every business day for 60 days after submission.
On receipt of any BMA notice, log it same-day in the Internal Regulatory System with the notice date and open a 14-day response countdown task.
Route the notice immediately to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and, for valuation content, the Appointed Actuary.
File the notice in the filing record.
checklist.done: every BMA notice is logged same-day with a 14-day countdown task and routed to its owner.

checklist.step: Answer BMA deficiency notices within 14 days
actions: Draft the response addressing each deficiency point, pulling corrected schedules from the owning team and actuarial answers from the Appointed Actuary.
Have the Compliance Officer clear the draft, including any acknowledgement of error, before it is sent.
Submit the response through the BMA portal or the channel the notice specifies within 14 days of the initial notification, and download proof of submission.
Log the response date against the countdown task and attach the response to the filing record.
checklist.done: the cleared response is submitted with proof inside 14 days of the initial notification and logged.

checklist.step: Refile corrected schedules where the BMA requires resubmission
actions: Correct the deficient schedule in the source package, re-running the cross-schedule consistency checks.
Where a corrected schedule changes reserve figures, obtain the Appointed Actuary's written confirmation that the opinion still stands or needs re-issue.
Resubmit through the portal within the window the BMA sets (14 days of the initial notification unless the notice states otherwise) and capture the new confirmation.
Version the refiled package as an amendment in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: corrected schedules are refiled in the BMA's window with actuarial confirmation and a versioned amendment archived.

checklist.step: Log and remediate filing exceptions
actions: Log any late filing, missing-opinion package, portal failure or 14-day miss in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with root cause and owner.
Assess with the Compliance Officer whether the failure is a material Code breach requiring self-report to the BMA with a remediation plan.
Track remediation to closure with CFO sign-off.
Feed root causes into next year's filing procedure update.
checklist.done: every exception is logged, assessed for self-report, remediated and signed off by the CFO.

checklist.step: Brief the Board on filing status
actions: Add the filing outcome — submission date versus deadline, notices received, responses made — to the next Board pack in the board portal.
Minute the Board's notation of the filing and any open BMA correspondence.
File the minute reference in the filing record.
checklist.done: the Board pack and minutes record the filing outcome and open correspondence.

checklist.step: Maintain portal access and submitter authorisations
actions: Review the BMA portal user list quarterly: remove leavers within 5 business days, confirm at least two authorised submitters remain.
Verify submitter contact details registered with the BMA are current so notices reach the team.
Record the review in the Internal Regulatory System.
Coordinate access changes with the Access Management Analyst.
checklist.done: a quarterly access review shows current submitters, no leavers and up-to-date BMA contact details.

checklist.step: Run the post-cycle debrief and update the procedure
actions: Hold a debrief with Statutory Reporting, Actuarial and Compliance within 30 days of filing: what slipped, which BMA instruction changes bit, which checks failed.
Update the BMA Annual Filing Procedure and package checklist with the findings.
Route the updated procedure to the CFO for re-approval.
File the debrief note and approved procedure in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a debrief note exists and the re-approved procedure reflects the cycle's lessons.

testing.step: Build the population of filings and BMA notices
actions: Extract from the Internal Regulatory System every BMA statutory filing record and every logged BMA notice for the review period.
Reconcile the filing list to the fiscal years requiring a filing — one SFR package per year, no gaps.
Cross-check the notice log against the registered correspondence inbox for unlogged BMA letters.
testing.done: the population covers every required filing and every BMA notice, with inbox cross-check complete.

testing.step: Reconcile as-filed packages to the archived source of record
actions: Compare the as-filed package in the financial reporting repository to the frozen pre-submission version — same schedules, same figures.
Confirm the archived portal confirmation timestamp matches the filing record's submission date.
Any post-freeze figure change without an amendment record is an exception.
testing.done: as-filed packages match frozen versions and confirmations match logged dates.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline and test timeliness
actions: Independently recompute each year's deadline as four months after fiscal year end from the entity's year-end date.
Compare the portal confirmation timestamp to the recomputed deadline.
Any submission after the deadline is a fail regardless of BMA tolerance shown.
testing.done: every filing pre-dates the independently recomputed deadline or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Verify the signed opinion was inside each filed package
actions: Open each as-filed package and locate the actuarial opinion at the position the BMA instructions specify.
Verify it is the signed, dated version by matching its version id to the document management repository record from REG-054-C02.
Agree the opined amounts to the reserve lines in the filed schedules to the dollar.
testing.done: each filed package contains the signed opinion, version-matched and amount-matched to the schedules.

testing.step: Trace declarations to authorised officers
actions: For each filing, trace every declaration signature to the officer register as at the signature date.
Verify DocuSign completion certificates exist and pre-date the portal submission.
A declaration signed by a person not on the register at that date is an exception.
testing.done: all declarations trace to then-current officers with completion certificates pre-dating submission.

testing.step: Re-perform the package completeness check
actions: Using the BMA's own instruction pack for each filing year (not the internal checklist), independently list the required schedules for the entity's licence class.
Tick each required schedule against the as-filed package.
Any schedule the BMA required but the package lacks is an exception, even if the BMA raised no deficiency.
testing.done: an independent completeness check against BMA instructions shows every required schedule filed.

testing.step: Recompute the 14-day clock on every BMA notice
actions: For each logged notice, compute notice date plus 14 days and compare to the evidenced response submission date.
Verify response proof (portal receipt or transmission record) exists for each response.
Any response after 14 days of the initial notification, or without proof, is a fail.
testing.done: every notice shows a proven response within the recomputed 14-day window or a logged fail.

testing.step: Verify compliance clearance on outbound responses
actions: For each deficiency response, locate the Compliance Officer's clearance record dated before the response was sent.
For responses touching valuation content, locate the Appointed Actuary's confirmation.
An uncleared response is a process exception even where content was accurate.
testing.done: every response shows pre-dated compliance clearance and actuarial confirmation where applicable.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the filing year or notice id, the requirement missed and the regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (calendar, package assembly, portal access, clearance) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Refer any late filing or missed 14-day response to the Compliance Officer for BMA self-report assessment.
Carry open items into next year's test.
testing.done: each exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and reportability referral.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off and reporting
actions: State the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) against the zero-tolerance thresholds with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer — segregated from Regulatory Reporting — sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee with the filing-cycle debrief.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C03.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to the Audit Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary runs the annual asset adequacy / cash-flow testing and produces the AAT report; the Appointed Actuary owns the conclusion; escalation to the Chief Actuary

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Bermuda Insurance Code of Conduct (August 2022) s.5/s.6 (risk management and internal controls over insurance liabilities) and the BMA EBS/BSCR guidance on scenario-based approaches; the current Code and BMA guidance are re-downloaded each cycle and cited in the AAT report's standards section

In-scope processes.value: Annual asset adequacy testing for the Bermuda entity's Life & Annuity liabilities: asset and liability data assembly, scenario set definition (including prescribed interest-rate paths), projection runs, reserve-adequacy conclusion, additional-reserve recommendation and AAT report production

In-scope systems.value: Projections in the actuarial modeling platform; asset holdings and cash-flow data from BlackRock Aladdin; the AAT report archived in the financial reporting repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Asset Adequacy Testing Procedure: annex to the Reserving Policy covering asset segmentation, scenario set (level, up, down, whipsaw and stochastic paths), reinvestment rules, moderately-adverse standard, and the report content list

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary with Board Risk Committee notation; reviewed annually and on any material change to the investment strategy or product mix

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: AAT complete and the report signed before the actuarial opinion is signed (REG-054-C02), which itself precedes the BMA Statutory Financial Return date four months after year end; interim refresh triggered by a 200bp rate move or material portfolio shift

Deadline reminders configured.value: Close calendar milestones at T-45/T-30/T-15 working days before the opinion signature date alerting the ALM Actuary and Appointed Actuary; rate-move trigger monitored monthly

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: AAT report, asset and liability extracts, scenario files, projection run logs and the additional-reserve decision retained 10 years in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed AAT cycle, unsupported scenario set, failed asset-liability reconciliation or an inadequacy left unreserved is logged in the regulatory filing/issue tracker and assessed as a potential material Code breach for BMA self-report

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off remediation of AAT exceptions; additional-reserve postings co-signed by the Chief Financial Officer

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The annual AAT report and its inputs for each year in the review period: asset extracts, liability model points, scenario files, projection outputs and the adequacy conclusion

Pass/fail thresholds.value: AAT must cover 100% of interest-sensitive liabilities; asset extract reconciles to the investment accounting records within 0.5%; every scenario in the procedure's set is run; any indicated inadequacy is reserved or formally justified — a miss on any of these fails

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs annually after the AAT report is signed, before the opinion cycle test closes

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit reviewer who performed no AAT modelling; actuarial re-performance assigned to an actuary outside the ALM team

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual AAT test workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C04, with run-log references and recomputation schedules

Regulator-ready documentation.value: AAT report with scenario results, asset listings and the adequacy conclusion retrievable for a BMA request within 14 days

Regulator response path.value: Appointed Actuary answers BMA questions on asset adequacy; the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary supplies scenario detail; correspondence routed via the Regulatory Reporting Manager

checklist.step: Scope the testing segments and confirm the timetable
actions: List the liability segments for testing (annuities, universal life, traditional life, disabled-life reserves) and confirm 100% of interest-sensitive liabilities are covered by agreeing segment reserves to the signed valuation summary.
Confirm the asset segmentation plan maps each liability segment to its supporting asset portfolio.
Set the run timetable backed off the opinion signature date with the T-45/T-30/T-15 milestones.
Record scope and timetable in the AAT file.
checklist.done: segments cover 100% of interest-sensitive reserves with a mapped asset plan and a calendared timetable.

checklist.step: Extract the supporting asset portfolio
actions: Extract from BlackRock Aladdin the holdings for each supporting portfolio as at the valuation date: CUSIP/ISIN, par, book and market value, coupon, maturity, call schedule, credit rating and asset class.
Export projected asset cash flows including call/prepayment behaviour under the base curve.
Deliver the extract with control totals (par, book value by portfolio) to the ALM Actuary.
File the extract and run parameters in the AAT file.
checklist.done: asset extracts with cash flows and control totals are delivered and filed.

checklist.step: Reconcile assets to the investment accounting records
actions: Agree the extract's book values by portfolio to the investment accounting balances in the ledger within the 0.5% tolerance.
Investigate differences with the Investment Operations Manager — trades in transit, accrual timing — and document each.
Confirm no asset is double-counted across segments by checking the segment mapping for overlaps.
Have the Controller countersign the reconciliation.
checklist.done: asset extracts reconcile to accounting records within tolerance with a countersigned schedule.

checklist.step: Assemble the liability model points and validate against the valuation
actions: Reuse the year-end valuation model points (REG-054-C01) for the AAT projections, loading them into FIS Prophet's ALM structure.
Reconcile model point reserves to the signed valuation summary by segment.
Document any AAT-specific adjustments (aggregation, in-force date shifts) with rationale.
Log file names, counts and checksums in the run log.
checklist.done: liability model points tie to the signed valuation with adjustments documented and logged.

checklist.step: Define and approve the scenario set
actions: Build the deterministic set per the procedure: level rates, gradual up (+300bp over 10 years), gradual down (−300bp floored), pop-up, pop-down and whipsaw paths from the valuation-date curve.
Generate the stochastic rate scenarios where the procedure requires them, recording generator version and seed.
Set reinvestment and disinvestment rules (target portfolio, spreads, borrowing limits) per the current investment strategy confirmed with the Portfolio Manager.
Obtain Chief Actuary approval of the scenario set and file the approval.
checklist.done: the full scenario set and reinvestment rules are documented, seeded and approved.

checklist.step: Run the projections for every scenario
actions: Execute the asset-liability projections in the actuarial modeling platform for each scenario and segment, using the approved model version from the model governance repository.
Capture run ids, scenario ids, model version and warnings in the run log.
Verify each run completed the full projection horizon (30+ years or to runoff) without truncation.
Export ending surplus / market value of surplus by scenario and segment to the results workbook.
checklist.done: every approved scenario is run to full horizon with logged run ids and exported results.

checklist.step: Analyse results and identify inadequacies
actions: Tabulate ending surplus by scenario and segment and flag every scenario with negative ending surplus.
Assess adequacy against the moderately-adverse standard in the procedure, documenting the judgement for borderline scenarios.
Quantify the additional reserve indicated where results fail the standard, with the calculation shown.
Compare results to prior year and explain material shifts (rate environment, portfolio changes, product mix).
checklist.done: results are tabulated with inadequacies flagged, quantified and year-over-year movements explained.

checklist.step: Decide and post any additional reserve
actions: Review the indicated inadequacy and decide the additional reserve, documenting the decision rationale against the moderately-adverse standard.
Where no reserve is posted despite adverse scenarios, write the formal justification into the AAT report.
Instruct the Senior Accountant to post any additional reserve to the ledger before the opinion is signed, with the CFO co-signing the posting.
Confirm the posted amount flows into the reserve balances the opinion covers.
checklist.done: the additional-reserve decision is documented and any posting is in the ledger before opinion signature.

checklist.step: Write the AAT report
actions: Draft the report to the procedure's content list: scope and segments, data and reconciliations, scenario definitions, reinvestment rules, results by scenario, adequacy conclusion, additional-reserve decision and limitations.
Cross-reference every figure to the results workbook and run log ids.
Include the asset reconciliation and liability validation as appendices.
Version the draft in the document management repository.
checklist.done: a versioned draft report covers the full content list with traceable figures.

checklist.step: Peer review the AAT work
actions: Assign a reviewing actuary outside the ALM team to re-check scenario construction against the procedure, spot-check projection inputs for two segments, and verify the adequacy conclusion follows from the results.
Re-foot the additional-reserve calculation independently.
Record comments and resolutions on the peer-review log and sign it.
Return the report for finalisation.
checklist.done: an independent peer-review log is signed with all comments resolved.

checklist.step: Obtain Appointed Actuary sign-off of the AAT report
actions: Review the final report and challenge the scenario judgements and the moderately-adverse assessment.
Sign and date the report ahead of the actuarial opinion signature so the opinion can rely on it.
Reference the AAT report and its conclusion in the actuarial memorandum (REG-054-C02).
Lock the signed report against edit.
checklist.done: the signed AAT report pre-dates the opinion and is referenced in the memorandum.

checklist.step: Archive the AAT evidence pack
actions: Assemble the pack: signed report, asset extracts and reconciliation, model point validation, scenario files with seeds, run logs, results workbook, peer-review log and reserve-posting evidence.
File it in the financial reporting repository under REG-054-C04/<year> with the 10-year retention label.
Verify the index is complete and every run id in the report resolves to a logged run.
Notify Compliance the pack is ready for testing.
checklist.done: a complete, indexed, retention-labelled AAT pack is archived.

checklist.step: Monitor interim triggers for an off-cycle refresh
actions: Monitor monthly the trigger conditions: a 200bp move in the reference curve since the last AAT, a material asset reallocation, or a large block transaction.
Log each monthly check with the observed curve move and portfolio status.
Where a trigger fires, schedule an off-cycle AAT refresh within 60 days and notify the Chief Actuary.
File the monitoring log quarterly.
checklist.done: monthly trigger checks are logged and any fired trigger has a scheduled refresh.

checklist.step: Report AAT results to risk governance
actions: Present the AAT conclusion, scenario results and any additional reserve to the Board Risk Committee at its pre-filing meeting.
Highlight scenarios approaching inadequacy and the management actions assumed.
Minute the committee's notation and file the minute reference in the AAT pack.
Share results with the Enterprise Risk Manager for the risk register update.
checklist.done: the Risk Committee minutes record the AAT results and the risk register is updated.

checklist.step: Log and remediate AAT exceptions
actions: Log any missed milestone, reconciliation break, unrun scenario or undocumented judgement in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with root cause and owner.
Route potential material Code breaches to the Compliance Officer for BMA self-report assessment.
Track remediation to closure with Chief Actuary sign-off.
Feed recurring causes into the next procedure review.
checklist.done: every exception is logged, assessed, remediated and signed off.

testing.step: Build the population of AAT cycles and inputs
actions: Pull each year's archived AAT pack from the financial reporting repository for the review period.
Confirm one signed AAT report exists per required annual cycle plus any trigger-driven refresh.
List the pack contents against the procedure's evidence list as the test inventory.
testing.done: every required cycle has a signed report and a content-listed pack.

testing.step: Reconcile tested liabilities to the source of record
actions: Agree the segment reserves tested in the AAT to the signed valuation summary and confirm coverage of 100% of interest-sensitive liabilities.
Identify any liability block excluded from testing and verify a documented exclusion rationale exists.
An untested interest-sensitive block without rationale is a fail.
testing.done: tested segments reconcile to the valuation with all exclusions documented.

testing.step: Re-verify the asset reconciliation
actions: Re-agree the asset extract book values to the investment accounting balances in SAP S/4HANA (GL) within the 0.5% tolerance.
Check the countersigned reconciliation and test two documented differences to support.
Check the segment mapping for double-counted assets by summing mapped portfolios against total invested assets.
testing.done: asset extracts re-reconcile within tolerance with no double-counting.

testing.step: Draw a sample of scenarios and segments
actions: Select the two largest segments plus one random segment (recorded seed), and within each, the level, worst adverse and one random scenario.
Record seed, population and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Include any scenario that produced negative ending surplus.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers large segments and every inadequate scenario.

testing.step: Re-perform sampled projection runs
actions: Re-run the sampled scenario/segment cells in the actuarial modeling platform from the archived model points, scenario files and model version recorded in the run log.
Compare ending surplus to the results workbook; differences beyond rounding are exceptions.
Capture re-run ids into the test workpaper.
testing.done: re-runs reproduce reported ending surplus for every sampled cell.

testing.step: Verify the scenario set against the procedure
actions: List the scenarios the procedure requires and tick each against the run log — level, up, down, pop-up, pop-down, whipsaw and any required stochastic set.
Verify the starting curve equals the valuation-date curve from the filed source download.
Verify stochastic seeds and generator versions were recorded; an unrecorded seed is an exception.
testing.done: every required scenario was run from the correct starting curve with recorded seeds.

testing.step: Recompute the additional-reserve arithmetic and posting
actions: Re-foot the indicated-inadequacy calculation from the scenario results.
Where a reserve was posted, trace the journal in the ledger, its CFO co-signature and that posting pre-dated the opinion signature.
Where no reserve was posted despite adverse results, verify the formal justification exists in the signed report.
testing.done: reserve arithmetic verifies and postings or justifications are evidenced and correctly sequenced.

testing.step: Verify sequencing against the opinion and filing
actions: Check the AAT report signature date precedes the actuarial opinion signature date, which precedes the BMA filing date.
Verify the actuarial memorandum references the AAT conclusion.
Check monthly trigger-monitoring logs exist and any fired trigger led to a refresh within 60 days.
testing.done: dates sequence correctly, the memorandum cross-references the AAT, and trigger monitoring is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the cycle, segment/scenario, control missed and impact on the adequacy conclusion.
Assign root cause (data, scenario governance, model version, sequencing) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Refer unreserved-inadequacy findings to the Compliance Officer for BMA self-report assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test.
testing.done: each exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and referral where required.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off and reporting
actions: State the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) against the coverage, reconciliation and scenario thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer — who performed no AAT modelling — sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee alongside the opinion-cycle test.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C04.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Land the quarter-end valuation extract with control totals
actions: Run the valuation extract pipeline from the Policy Administration Platform into the enterprise data warehouse as at quarter end, by working day 2.
Emit control totals with the run id: policy count, sum assured, account value and annualised premium by product line and status.
Publish the run id and totals to the Reserving Analyst and Data Quality Analyst.
Store the pipeline log against the run id.
checklist.done: the extract is landed by WD+2 with a run id and published control totals.

checklist.step: Pull the admin-system control report for the same date
actions: Generate the Policy Administration Platform's own period-end inforce control report for the identical as-at date, using the same status definitions as the extract.
Export counts and amounts by product line and status to the reconciliation workbook.
Confirm with the Policy Admin Ops Lead that all quarter-end batch processing (terminations, maturities, reinstatements) completed before the report was cut.
File the report with its generation timestamp.
checklist.done: the source control report for the same date and status basis is exported and timestamped.

checklist.step: Run the automated data-quality rules on the extract
actions: Execute the valuation rule set in the data catalog/quality tool: null checks on plan code/issue date/status, valid-value checks on product codes, duplicate policy detection, and negative-value screens on account values.
Review the rule results and classify each failure as blocking (fix before load) or non-blocking (document and monitor).
Return blocking failures to the Data Engineer for re-extract or source correction.
Attach the rule-run report to the reconciliation workbook.
checklist.done: the rule set has run with every failure classified and blocking items returned for fix.

checklist.step: Compare control totals and compute differences
actions: In the reconciliation workbook, compare extract totals to the admin control report by product line and status: count, sum assured, account value, premium.
Compute absolute and percentage differences per cell against the 0.5% tolerance.
Colour-flag every out-of-tolerance cell and list it on the break log with a unique break id.
Save the versioned workbook to the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: cell-level differences are computed with every out-of-tolerance cell on the break log.

checklist.step: Roll the inforce forward from prior quarter
actions: Build the roll-forward per product line: opening count + new business − deaths − surrenders − maturities − lapses ± reinstatements = closing count.
Source movement counts from the Policy Administration Platform's transaction summary for the quarter.
Compare the derived closing count to the extract count and add any residual over tolerance to the break log.
Record the roll-forward in the reconciliation workbook.
checklist.done: the roll-forward reconciles movements to the closing position with residuals within tolerance or logged.

checklist.step: Investigate breaks down the resolution ladder
actions: Work each break id down the ladder: as-at-date mismatch, status-mapping difference, late-processed transactions, extract filter error, then genuine source-data defect.
For each break record cause, affected policies (drill to policy number where possible), dollar impact and the correcting action.
Route source-data defects to the Policy Administration Analyst for correction in the admin system, not in the extract.
Escalate any break unresolved by WD+4 to the Chief Data Officer.
checklist.done: every break has a cause, impact, correcting action and owner, with WD+4 escalations made.

checklist.step: Quantify the reserve impact of unresolved breaks
actions: For breaks that will not clear before model load, estimate the reserve impact using per-policy average reserves for the affected product line.
Decide accept / adjust / block: accept immaterial breaks with documented rationale, post a valuation adjustment for estimable impacts, block the load for material unquantifiable breaks.
Record the decision per break id on the break log.
Notify the Appointed Actuary of any accepted break above 0.1% of line reserves.
checklist.done: every unresolved break carries a quantified impact and a documented accept/adjust/block decision.

checklist.step: Countersign the reconciliation before model load
actions: Verify the workbook shows: totals compared, roll-forward complete, rule-run attached, every break dispositioned.
Countersign the reconciliation with date and time, by working day 5.
Obtain the Reserving Analyst's counter-signature as the second check.
Release the extract run id to the Actuarial Analyst for model point build — the load may not start earlier.
checklist.done: a dual-signed reconciliation dated by WD+5 releases the extract for model load.

checklist.step: Publish the quarterly reconciliation report
actions: Compile the reconciliation report: control-total comparison, roll-forward, rule results, break log with dispositions and the dual signatures.
File it in the financial reporting repository under REG-054-C05/<quarter> with the 10-year retention label.
Send the report link to the Valuation Actuary, Chief Data Officer and Compliance Analyst.
Index the report against the extract run id used for the valuation.
checklist.done: the filed report is indexed to the run id and distributed to the named recipients.

checklist.step: Track aged breaks to closure
actions: Carry every open break into the regulatory filing/issue tracker with its break id, cause, impact and owner.
Review open breaks weekly with the Policy Administration Analyst until the source correction lands.
Verify each closure in the next quarter's extract — the break must not recur for the same policies.
Flag any break aged past one quarter to the Chief Data Officer for remediation sign-off.
checklist.done: open breaks are tracked weekly, verified closed in the next extract, and aged items escalated.

checklist.step: Reconcile reserve output back to the data used
actions: After the valuation run, reconcile model point counts and amounts in the run log back to the released extract's control totals.
Confirm no policies were added, dropped or altered between release and model load by comparing checksums.
Record the end-to-end tie-out (admin report → extract → model points → reserve run) in the valuation workpaper pack.
Report any post-release change as an incident to the Data Quality Analyst.
checklist.done: an end-to-end tie-out shows the reserves were computed on exactly the released, reconciled data.

checklist.step: Review status and product mapping tables quarterly
actions: Review the product-code and status mapping tables in Enterprise Reference Data (MDM/RDM) against new plan codes launched in the quarter.
Add mappings for any new plan code before the next extract; an unmapped code must fail the data-quality rules, not silently drop.
Version the mapping table and record the review date.
Notify the Data Engineer of mapping changes affecting the pipeline.
checklist.done: mapping tables cover every live plan code with a versioned, dated review.

checklist.step: Test the pipeline after any admin-system or ETL change
actions: On any Policy Administration Platform release or ETL change, run the extract pipeline against a pre-release copy and compare control totals to the last production run in the data pipeline orchestrator.
Investigate any shift in totals beyond expected business movement before promoting the change.
Record the regression comparison in the change ticket.
Inform the Data Quality Analyst that the change is cleared for the next quarter-end run.
checklist.done: every pipeline-affecting change carries a recorded regression comparison before production use.

checklist.step: Report reconciliation health to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the data governance forum: on-time completion, break counts and aging, tolerance breaches and repeat causes.
Table systemic fixes (source defects, mapping gaps) with owners and dates.
Minute the forum's decisions and file the minutes with the reconciliation report.
Share the summary with the Chief Actuary for the valuation governance pack.
checklist.done: governance minutes record the quarter's reconciliation health and systemic fixes with owners.

checklist.step: Log exceptions and capture remediation sign-off
actions: Log any model load on unreconciled data, missed WD+5 signature or tolerance breach accepted without rationale in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
Assign root cause and owner; obtain Chief Data Officer sign-off on closure, with Chief Actuary co-sign where reserves were affected.
Assess repeated failures with the Compliance Officer as a potential Code s.6 control weakness for BMA self-report.
Retain the exception records with the quarterly report.
checklist.done: control failures are logged, signed off on closure and assessed for reportability.

testing.step: Build the population of quarterly reconciliations
actions: Pull every reconciliation report filed under REG-054-C05 for the review period from the financial reporting repository.
Confirm one report per quarter with no gaps against the valuation calendar.
List the extract run ids each report covers as the test inventory.
testing.done: a complete quarter-by-quarter population with run ids is inventoried.

testing.step: Reconcile reports to the valuation actually run
actions: Match each quarter's released run id to the run id recorded in the valuation run log (REG-054-C01).
A valuation run on a different or unreleased run id is an automatic exception.
Record the match table in the workpaper.
testing.done: every valuation traces to the released, reconciled extract or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of quarters and cells
actions: Select two quarters (latest plus one random with recorded seed) and within each, the three largest product lines plus two random cells.
Include every cell that breached tolerance in the period.
Record seed, population size and selection date for re-drawability.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers large lines, random cells and all tolerance breaches.

testing.step: Re-perform the control-total comparison from source
actions: Independently regenerate the Policy Administration Platform inforce control report for the sampled as-at dates.
Recompute the differences against the archived extract totals without reference to the filed workbook.
Compare to the reported differences; any discrepancy in the reconciliation itself is an exception.
testing.done: independently regenerated source totals reproduce the reported differences.

testing.step: Recompute the roll-forward arithmetic
actions: Re-foot the sampled roll-forwards: opening + new business − terminations ± reinstatements = closing.
Agree movement counts to the admin system's transaction summary for the quarter.
Verify residuals were within tolerance or listed on the break log.
testing.done: roll-forward arithmetic verifies against source transaction counts.

testing.step: Test break dispositions to evidence
actions: For ten sampled break ids (or all, if fewer), verify cause, quantified impact and the accept/adjust/block decision are recorded.
For source-defect breaks, trace the correction into the admin system and confirm non-recurrence in the following quarter's extract.
A break accepted without quantified impact or aged past one quarter without CDO escalation is a fail.
testing.done: sampled breaks show evidenced dispositions, source corrections and non-recurrence.

testing.step: Verify signature timing and load sequencing
actions: Check each sampled quarter's dual countersignature is dated by WD+5 and before the model load timestamp in the run log.
Any load that started before release is a fail regardless of eventual reconciliation outcome.
Record the date chain (extract → signatures → load) in the workpaper.
testing.done: the date chain proves reconciliation and release preceded every model load.

testing.step: Test the data-quality rule coverage
actions: Review the rule set in the data catalog/quality tool against the standard's required checks (nulls, valid values, duplicates, negatives).
Inspect the sampled quarters' rule-run reports for blocking failures released without fix.
Verify unmapped plan codes fail the rules by checking a quarter where a new product launched.
testing.done: the rule set matches the standard and blocking failures were never released unfixed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the quarter, cell or break id, control missed and reserve impact.
Assign root cause (timing, mapping, source defect, discipline) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Refer systemic control weaknesses to the Compliance Officer for Code s.6 reportability assessment.
Carry open items into the next quarterly test.
testing.done: each exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and referral where systemic.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off
actions: State the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) against the countersignature, tolerance and aging thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Data and Actuarial — sign the workpaper.
Report quarterly results to the data governance forum and annually to the Audit Committee.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C05.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported to governance.
