checklist.step: Log every BMA valuation inquiry on the day it arrives
actions: On receipt of a BMA letter, portal message or email touching reserves, the opinion or AAT, create an inquiry record in the Internal Regulatory System the same business day.
Capture: notice date, channel, BMA reference number, cited statutory provision, questions asked and any stated deadline.
Set the response deadline: the BMA's stated date, or 14 days from the initial notification where none is stated, and start the countdown task.
Attach the inbound document to the record and open the correspondence file in the document management repository.
checklist.done: the inquiry is logged same-day with deadline, countdown and an opened correspondence file.

checklist.step: Route the inquiry to the owning actuary and assemble the team
actions: Notify the Appointed Actuary and Chief Actuary within one business day with the logged record link.
Assign a drafting owner per question — Valuation Actuary for reserve mechanics, ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary for AAT, Capital Model Actuary for risk margin/BSCR points.
Alert the Compliance Officer and, where the letter alleges or implies a breach, the General Counsel immediately.
Record assignments and the internal draft-due date (day 7) on the inquiry record.
checklist.done: owners are assigned with a day-7 internal due date and legal alerted where breach is implied.

checklist.step: Freeze and gather the source records the inquiry touches
actions: Pull from the financial reporting repository the exact archived packs the inquiry concerns: valuation workpapers (REG-054-C01), signed opinion file (REG-054-C02), filed SFR package (REG-054-C03), AAT pack (REG-054-C04).
Place a legal-hold flag on those records so nothing is edited or purged while the inquiry is open.
Index the pulled records in the correspondence file.
Note any record the inquiry needs that cannot be located — escalate that gap to the Compliance Officer the same day.
checklist.done: source records are pulled, legal-held and indexed, with any gap escalated same-day.

checklist.step: Draft answers from the archived record, not from memory
actions: Answer each BMA question by citing the archived pack — run ids, workpaper page references and filed schedule lines — so every figure in the draft traces to evidence.
Reconcile any figure quoted in the response to the filed SFR package to the dollar; explain, never paper over, differences from what was filed.
Keep the draft to the questions asked; list any volunteered context separately for the clearance chain to rule on.
Save the draft with version control in the correspondence file by day 7.
checklist.done: a day-7 draft answers each question with evidence references and reconciled figures.

checklist.step: Decide on an extension before day 7 where the deadline is unachievable
actions: At the day-7 checkpoint, assess whether a complete, cleared response will be ready by the deadline.
Where it will not, draft an extension request stating the reason and a committed date, and have the Compliance Officer approve it.
Submit the extension request to the BMA before day 7 through the same channel as the inquiry, and log the BMA's answer.
Update the countdown task to any granted date; a silent or refused extension leaves the 14-day clock in force.
checklist.done: the deadline is either achievable or an approved extension request was submitted before day 7 with the outcome logged.

checklist.step: Run actuarial review of the draft
actions: Review the draft for technical accuracy and consistency with the signed opinion and memorandum — the response must not contradict the filed record without saying so explicitly.
Where the inquiry has exposed a genuine error in filed figures, state the error, its size and the correction plan rather than obscuring it.
Sign the actuarial clearance on the inquiry record by day 10.
Return unresolved technical points to the drafting owner with a same-week turnaround.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary's clearance is recorded by day 10 with any filed-record error explicitly handled.

checklist.step: Run compliance and legal clearance
actions: Review the cleared draft for tone, completeness against every question asked, and consistency with prior BMA correspondence in the file.
Route to the General Counsel any passage admitting a breach, error or Code non-compliance, and incorporate counsel's wording.
Confirm the volunteered-context list — include or withhold each item with a recorded reason.
Sign compliance clearance on the inquiry record by day 10.
checklist.done: compliance clearance is recorded by day 10 with legal wording on any admission.

checklist.step: Submit the response and capture proof
actions: Submit the final response through the channel the BMA used or specified — portal upload or addressed letter — by day 13, inside the 14-day window or the granted extension.
Capture proof of submission: portal receipt, or the transmission record with date and addressee.
File the as-sent response and proof in the correspondence file and close the countdown task with the actual response date.
Send the as-sent copy to the Appointed Actuary, Compliance Officer and General Counsel.
checklist.done: the response is submitted in-window with proof filed and the countdown closed on the actual date.

checklist.step: Handle BMA follow-ups as linked child inquiries
actions: Log any BMA follow-up question as a child record linked to the parent inquiry, with its own 14-days-from-notification clock.
Run the same draft-clear-submit chain, reusing the frozen source records.
Keep the correspondence file chronological across parent and children.
Close the parent only when the BMA confirms the matter is resolved or 90 days pass with no further contact.
checklist.done: follow-ups are clocked and cleared as child records and the parent closes on confirmed resolution.

checklist.step: Execute commitments made in responses
actions: Extract every commitment made to the BMA in the response — corrected schedules, methodology changes, additional reserves, future disclosures — onto a commitment list with owners and dates.
Track each commitment in the regulatory filing/issue tracker to completion.
Evidence completion in the correspondence file (for example the refiled schedule confirmation under REG-054-C03).
Report open commitments monthly to the Compliance Officer until done.
checklist.done: every commitment to the BMA is tracked, evidenced complete and reported until closed.

checklist.step: Maintain the correspondence file to the standard
actions: Keep the file chronological and complete: inbound letter, log entry, drafts with versions, clearance records, extension correspondence, as-sent response, proof, follow-ups and the commitment list.
Apply the 10-year retention label and the REG-054-C06 index tag on closure.
Verify no document exists outside the file — sweep the team mailbox for stray BMA emails and file them.
Release the legal hold on source packs once the inquiry closes.
checklist.done: a complete chronological file is retention-labelled with the mailbox swept and holds released.

checklist.step: Brief governance on open inquiries
actions: Report open BMA valuation inquiries, deadlines and themes to the quarterly compliance committee and, for material matters, the Audit Committee.
Flag any inquiry implying a solvency or opinion concern to the Board via the Corporate Secretary without waiting for the cycle.
Minute the reporting and file the minute reference on each inquiry record.
checklist.done: governance minutes record open inquiries with material matters escalated to the Board.

checklist.step: Sweep channels for unlogged BMA contacts
actions: Monthly, sweep the BMA portal message centre, the registered-office correspondence log and the actuarial team mailboxes for BMA contacts not in the Internal Regulatory System.
Log any find retroactively with its true notice date and treat an already-blown clock as a reportable exception, not a reset.
Remind staff quarterly that any direct BMA contact must reach the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day.
Record each sweep with date and result.
checklist.done: monthly sweeps are recorded and any unlogged contact is logged at its true date and flagged.

checklist.step: Log and remediate handling exceptions
actions: Log late responses, missed clearances, unlogged contacts and unmet commitments in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with root cause and owner.
Assess a pattern of lateness as a Code business-conduct issue and decide on BMA self-report with the General Counsel.
Sign off each remediation on closure, with Chief Actuary co-sign for content errors.
Feed causes into the annual procedure review.
checklist.done: handling exceptions are logged, assessed for reportability and signed off on closure.

checklist.step: Run the annual inquiry-readiness drill
actions: Annually, run a mock BMA valuation inquiry: draft a realistic question set, start the clock and run intake-to-submission against the procedure.
Time each stage against the day 3/7/10/13 milestones and note failures.
Debrief with Actuarial, Compliance and Legal and update the procedure with fixes.
File the drill record in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: an annual timed drill is filed with debrief actions in the procedure.

testing.step: Build the population of inquiries including unlogged contacts
actions: Extract every valuation-related inquiry record from the Internal Regulatory System for the half-year.
Independently sweep the BMA portal message centre, registered-office log and actuarial mailboxes for BMA contacts absent from the system.
Add any unlogged contact to the population at its true notice date as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population covers logged inquiries plus independently discovered contacts.

testing.step: Reconcile correspondence files to the log
actions: For each inquiry, open the correspondence file in the document management repository and check it against the standard's content list.
Verify the as-sent response and proof of submission are present.
A file missing the inbound letter, a clearance record or submission proof is an exception.
testing.done: every inquiry has a complete correspondence file or a logged gap.

testing.step: Recompute every response clock
actions: For each inquiry, compute the deadline independently: the BMA's stated date, else notice date plus 14 days of the initial notification.
Compare the proven submission date to the recomputed deadline, crediting only extensions granted in writing before day 7.
Any late response is a fail; a 'granted' extension without the BMA's written answer on file counts as refused.
testing.done: every response is proven in-window against an independently recomputed clock or logged as a fail.

testing.step: Verify same-day logging discipline
actions: Compare each record's system creation timestamp to the notice date on the inbound document.
Flag records created more than one business day after receipt.
Cross-check the monthly sweep records exist for every month in the period.
testing.done: logging lag is measured for every inquiry and sweep evidence covers all months.

testing.step: Trace response figures to the archived record
actions: Draw a sample of three inquiries (all, if fewer) and trace every figure in each as-sent response to the archived valuation, opinion or AAT pack by run id or page reference.
Re-agree quoted figures to the filed SFR package to the dollar.
An untraceable or unreconciled figure in a sent response is a content exception for Chief Actuary review.
testing.done: sampled response figures trace to archived evidence and agree to the filed record.

testing.step: Verify the clearance chain on every response
actions: Check each response shows Appointed Actuary and Compliance Officer clearances dated before submission.
For responses containing an admission of error or breach, verify General Counsel wording clearance is on file.
An uncleared submission is a fail regardless of content accuracy.
testing.done: every submission shows pre-dated clearances, with legal clearance on admissions.

testing.step: Test commitment tracking to completion
actions: Re-read each as-sent response and independently extract the commitments made to the BMA.
Match each to a tracker item and verify completion evidence in the correspondence file.
A commitment absent from the tracker, or past-due without escalation, is an exception.
testing.done: independently extracted commitments all trace to tracked, evidenced completion.

testing.step: Verify follow-up and closure handling
actions: Check follow-ups were logged as child records with their own recomputed clocks.
Verify parents closed only on confirmed resolution or the 90-day quiet period.
Verify legal holds on source packs were applied at intake and released at closure.
testing.done: follow-ups carry their own clocks and closures and holds follow the procedure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the inquiry reference, requirement missed and regulatory exposure.
Assign root cause (intake, drafting, clearance, submission, tracking) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Refer lateness patterns and unlogged contacts to the Compliance Officer for Code self-report assessment.
Carry open items into the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: each exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and referral where warranted.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off and reporting
actions: State the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Regulatory Reporting and Actuarial — sign the workpaper.
Report to the compliance committee with the inquiry themes observed.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C06.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

Have the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager approve every matrix version.
Publish the current version link to the Policy Forms Specialist and Product teams.
checklist.done: an approved, versioned matrix maps every Code disclosure to content, trigger, timing and document types.

checklist.step: Build and maintain the form inventory
actions: List every live customer-facing template in OpenText Document Mgmt: form id, edition date, document type, products used on, generating system and the matrix rows it satisfies.
Reconcile the inventory quarterly against the templates actually configured in the policy administration system — anything generating documents but absent from the inventory is added immediately.
Mark superseded editions as retired with their retirement date.
Version the inventory and record the quarterly review date.
checklist.done: a versioned inventory covers every generating template, reconciled quarterly to the admin system.

checklist.step: Map every matrix requirement to carrying templates
actions: Cross-map each matrix row to the inventory templates that carry it, recording the section/page where the wording sits.
Flag any matrix row with no carrying template as a coverage gap and open a build task with a due date inside the 90-day window.
Flag any template carrying stale wording against the current matrix version.
Review the map with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager monthly until gaps close.
checklist.done: every matrix row maps to live templates or an open, dated build task; stale wording is flagged.

checklist.step: Intake each change that touches customer documents
actions: Open a change case in the workflow/case management tool for every product change, Code amendment or correction affecting customer documents.
Record the driver, affected products, affected templates from the inventory and the matrix rows implicated.
Set the remediation deadline: before the next customer send of the affected template or 90 days, whichever is sooner.
Assign the Policy Forms Specialist as drafting owner.
checklist.done: every document-affecting change has a case with affected templates, matrix rows and a deadline.

checklist.step: Draft the disclosure wording to the standard
actions: Draft the wording in the master template in OpenText Document Mgmt, meeting the matrix row's content, prominence and placement rules (font size, position before signature blocks, headed sections).
Produce a redline against the current approved edition.
Check plain-language standards — reading level, defined terms, no burying material terms in footnotes.
Version the draft and link it to the change case.
checklist.done: a versioned redlined draft meets the matrix row's content and prominence rules.

checklist.step: Obtain wording review from the coverage specialist
actions: Review the draft for consistency with the policy's coverage terms — the disclosure must not contradict the contract wording.
Check defined terms match the policy definitions exactly.
Record review comments on the change case and clear them with the Policy Forms Specialist.
Sign the wording review on the case.
checklist.done: a signed wording review confirms the disclosure is consistent with the contract terms.

checklist.step: Obtain compliance approval of the final wording
actions: Verify the final draft satisfies the quoted Code paragraph on the matrix row — content, trigger, timing and prominence.
Confirm the wording works for every product and channel the template serves.
Sign compliance approval on the change case; no template releases without it.
Update the matrix map with the new edition reference.
checklist.done: compliance approval is signed and the matrix map points at the approved edition.

checklist.step: Configure the approved template in the generating system
actions: Load the approved master into the policy administration system's document templates, mapping merge fields (policy number, values, dates) per the template specification.
Set the trigger rules so the document generates on the matrix row's trigger event for the in-scope products only.
Set the effective date and configure the superseded edition to retire on the same date.
Record the configuration change ticket against the change case.
checklist.done: the approved template is configured with correct triggers, merge fields and a same-day retirement of the old edition.

checklist.step: Test document generation before release
actions: In the test environment, generate the document for at least three policy scenarios per product (new issue, mid-term change, renewal or surrender as applicable).
Compare each output to the approved master: wording verbatim, prominence intact, merge fields populated correctly, no truncation across page breaks.
Verify the trigger fires on the right events and not on out-of-scope products.
Attach the test evidence to the change case and sign the test record.
checklist.done: signed generation tests show verbatim wording and correct triggers across the scenario set.

checklist.step: Release to production through the go-live gate
actions: Verify the gate conditions on the change case: wording review signed, compliance approval signed, generation tests passed, retirement of the old edition configured.
Schedule the production release and confirm post-release that the first generated documents use the new edition.
Update the form inventory with the new edition and the old edition's retirement date.
Close the change case with the release date.
checklist.done: the gate held, production generates the new edition, and inventory reflects the change.

checklist.step: Sweep for documents issued on superseded wording
actions: After each release, query the policy administration system's document log for any document generated on the retired edition after its retirement date.
List affected customers with document type and send date.
Pass the list to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for impact assessment and any corrective mailing.
File the sweep result on the change case.
checklist.done: a post-release sweep proves no superseded-edition sends, or affected customers are listed for remediation.

checklist.step: Remediate disclosure defects with customer impact
actions: Log each defect (missing disclosure, stale wording, wrong trigger) in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with the affected customer count and period.
Decide the remediation: corrective mailing with the compliant disclosure, reissue of documents, or documented no-harm rationale.
Execute corrective mailings within 30 days of the defect being confirmed and retain send evidence.
Obtain Head of Compliance sign-off on closure and assess material defects for BMA self-report.
checklist.done: every defect is logged, remediated or justified, signed off and assessed for reportability.

checklist.step: Control ad-hoc correspondence wording
actions: Use only approved paragraph blocks from the template library for ad-hoc customer letters touching matrix topics (surrender values, charges, complaints handling).
Route any free-text passage on a matrix topic to the Compliance Analyst for approval before sending.
Log approved ad-hoc wording so recurring passages get promoted into standard templates.
Never edit disclosure blocks locally.
checklist.done: ad-hoc letters use approved blocks, free-text on matrix topics is pre-approved, and recurring text is promoted.

checklist.step: Train forms and servicing staff on the disclosure regime
actions: Run annual training in the learning management system for forms, configuration and servicing staff on the matrix, the build procedure and the no-local-edit rule.
Include the current year's Code changes and defect lessons.
Track completion to 100% of in-scope staff within the assignment window and chase non-completers.
Retain completion records with the training content version.
checklist.done: annual training reaches 100% of in-scope staff with retained completion records.

checklist.step: Report disclosure-control health to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the compliance committee: matrix coverage, open gaps and their age, defects found, corrective mailings and remediation status.
Escalate any gap past its 90-day window with the reason and revised date.
Minute the reporting and file the minutes in the compliance evidence repository.
Confirm annually to the Board that customer disclosures comply with the Code.
checklist.done: quarterly governance reporting and an annual Board confirmation are minuted and filed.

testing.step: Build the population of templates and released changes
actions: Pull the current form inventory from OpenText Document Mgmt and every change case released in the half-year.
Independently query the policy administration system for all live document templates and reconcile against the inventory.
Any generating template absent from the inventory joins the population as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the population covers the reconciled inventory plus all released changes, with unlisted templates flagged.

testing.step: Reconcile the matrix to the current Code text
actions: Independently read the current Insurance Code of Conduct disclosure provisions and list the obligations.
Compare the list to the matrix rows; a Code obligation with no matrix row is a coverage exception.
Verify Code amendments in the period reached the matrix within 10 business days by comparing amendment dates to matrix version dates.
testing.done: the matrix independently covers the current Code with amendment lag inside 10 days.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of templates and requirements
actions: Select 10 matrix rows spanning the trigger events (application, issue, renewal, surrender, complaint) plus every row flagged as a gap in the period.
Select 10 templates: the 5 highest-volume by documents generated plus 5 random (recorded seed).
Record seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample spans triggers, gaps, high-volume and random templates.

testing.step: Re-perform the wording check on generated documents
actions: For each sampled template, pull three real documents generated in the period from the policy administration system document log.
Compare the disclosure wording verbatim to the approved master edition current at the generation date.
Check prominence rules held in the output — placement, size, no truncation.
Any deviation from the approved master is an exception.
testing.done: real generated documents carry the approved wording verbatim with prominence intact.

testing.step: Verify trigger correctness against events
actions: For 5 sampled matrix rows, pull policy events of the trigger type from the period and verify the required document generated for each.
Run the inverse check: confirm the document did not generate for out-of-scope products.
A trigger event without its document, or a wrong-product send, is an exception.
testing.done: trigger events produced their documents and out-of-scope products received none.

testing.step: Trace released changes through the approval chain
actions: For every change case released in the half-year, verify the chain in the workflow/case management tool: wording review signed, compliance approval signed, generation tests attached, all pre-dating release.
Verify the old edition's retirement date equals the new edition's effective date.
A release with any missing or post-dated sign-off is a fail.
testing.done: every release shows a complete, correctly sequenced approval chain and clean edition handover.

testing.step: Recompute remediation windows on gaps and defects
actions: For each coverage gap and defect in the period, recompute the deadline (next customer send or 90 days; corrective mailings 30 days from confirmation).
Compare actual closure dates to recomputed deadlines.
Verify superseded-edition sweeps ran after each release and affected-customer lists reached compliance.
testing.done: gap and defect closures meet recomputed windows and post-release sweeps are evidenced.

testing.step: Test ad-hoc correspondence controls
actions: Sample 10 ad-hoc customer letters from the period touching matrix topics.
Verify each used approved paragraph blocks or carries a pre-send Compliance Analyst approval.
Un-approved free-text on a matrix topic is an exception with customer-impact referral.
testing.done: sampled ad-hoc letters used approved wording or pre-send approvals.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the template or matrix row, requirement missed and customer impact.
Assign root cause (matrix lag, mapping, configuration, discipline) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Refer customer-impacting defects to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager for corrective-mailing and self-report assessment.
Carry open items into the next semi-annual test.
testing.done: each exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and impact referral.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off and reporting
actions: State the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) against the coverage and dual-sign-off thresholds.
Have the independent reviewer — outside forms and compliance — sign the workpaper.
Report to the compliance committee with defect themes.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C07.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion is filed and reported.

checklist.step: Maintain the notice SLA table
actions: Keep one SLA row per notice type in the requirements repository: trigger event, day count from trigger (14 days where the Code or the procedure sets 14; contractual counts elsewhere), delivery channel rules and the template id from the form inventory (REG-054-C07).
Source each day count to the Code paragraph or policy provision it comes from, quoted on the row.
Version the table and approve every change before configuration.
Publish the current version to the Policy Admin Ops Lead and Configuration Engineer.
checklist.done: an approved, versioned SLA table sources every notice type's day count and channel to its requirement.

checklist.step: Configure trigger detection for every SLA row
actions: Configure the Policy Administration Platform so each SLA-table trigger event (premium due, lapse warning, surrender confirmation, maturity, assignment, complaint acknowledgement) raises a notice task automatically with the trigger date stamped.
Map each trigger to the current approved template id and the SLA day count.
Test each trigger in the pre-production environment with event injection and verify the stamped trigger date equals the event date.
Record the configuration against the SLA table version.
checklist.done: every SLA row has a tested automatic trigger stamping the true event date.

checklist.step: Run the daily notice generation batch
actions: Run (or verify the schedule ran) the daily notice generation batch in the Policy Administration Platform, composing documents for all open notice tasks.
Review the batch completion report: tasks in, documents composed, failures out.
Requeue composition failures the same day after fixing the cause (missing data field, template error).
Post the day's control totals to the batch-control log.
checklist.done: the daily batch is verified complete with failures requeued same-day and totals logged.

checklist.step: Verify address and channel quality before dispatch
actions: Screen the day's dispatch file against address-quality rules: no blank or known-bad postal addresses, valid e-mail for e-delivery consents, returned-mail flags respected.
Divert failures to the exception queue and task the Life Policy Service Representative to obtain a corrected address within 5 business days.
Never silently drop a notice for address failure — the SLA clock keeps running and the exception stays open until delivered.
Record diverted counts on the batch-control log.
checklist.done: the dispatch file is screened, failures are diverted with tasks, and no notice is silently dropped.

checklist.step: Dispatch by the customer's delivery channel and capture evidence
actions: Release print/mail files to the mail house and e-delivery files to the customer portal/email service per each customer's recorded channel election.
Capture the dispatch manifest: notice id, policy number, channel, dispatch timestamp.
Archive the exact document copy sent into OpenText Document Mgmt linked to the notice id.
Import mail-house confirmation files and e-delivery send receipts daily.
checklist.done: every notice has a manifest entry, an archived copy and a channel confirmation.

checklist.step: Write every notice to the notice log with its day count
actions: Feed the notice log daily: notice id, type, policy number, trigger date, SLA day count, composition date, dispatch date and computed days-taken.
Compute the SLA flag per row (met / breached) in the BI/reporting platform.
Reconcile daily log inserts to the batch-control totals — composed minus failures equals logged.
Publish the daily aging view (pending notices at 50%/80% of day count) to the Policy Admin Ops Lead.
checklist.done: the log carries every notice with computed days-taken and reconciles to batch totals daily.

checklist.step: Work the aging queue before day counts expire
actions: Review the 50% and 80% aging alerts each morning and assign every pending notice a same-day action.
Prioritise 14-day notice types past day 7 and any notice within 3 days of its deadline.
Clear blockers directly with the Configuration Engineer (template faults) or Life Policy Service Representative (address chases).
Record actions on the aging queue so the trail shows intervention before breach.
checklist.done: aging alerts are actioned daily with documented interventions ahead of deadlines.

checklist.step: Handle returned mail and failed e-delivery
actions: Work the returned-mail and bounced-email queue daily: trace a better address via the policy file, recent payments or the agent of record.
Redispatch the notice to the corrected address within 5 business days of the failure and record the redispatch on the notice log.
After two failed attempts, apply the undeliverable procedure — flag the policy, hold non-essential mail, and record the diligence trail.
Update the customer record so future notices use the corrected address.
checklist.done: delivery failures are chased, redispatched inside 5 days, and undeliverables carry a diligence trail.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate SLA breaches same-day
actions: On any breach flag, dispatch the late notice immediately — lateness never converts to abandonment.
Log the breach in the regulatory filing/issue tracker with notice type, days late, cause and customer impact.
Notify the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager same-day for impact assessment (for example a lapse notice sent late must extend the customer's remedy window accordingly).
Track the remediation to closure with COO sign-off for systemic causes.
checklist.done: every breach is dispatched late-but-sent, logged, impact-assessed and remediated with sign-off.

checklist.step: Reconcile trigger events to notices weekly
actions: Weekly, extract all SLA-table trigger events from the policy administration transaction data in the enterprise data warehouse.
Match each event to a notice-log entry; list unmatched events as missed-notice candidates.
Investigate candidates within 2 business days — misconfigured trigger, suppressed task, data gap — and generate the missing notice immediately.
File the weekly reconciliation with its unmatched count and resolutions.
checklist.done: a weekly event-to-notice reconciliation exists with every unmatched event resolved and dispatched.

checklist.step: Re-test triggers after every admin-system release
actions: After each Policy Administration Platform release, re-run the trigger injection tests for every SLA row in pre-production.
Verify trigger firing, date stamping, template selection and day-count mapping are unchanged.
Block promotion of any release that breaks a trigger until fixed.
Attach test evidence to the release ticket.
checklist.done: post-release trigger tests pass for every SLA row with evidence on the release ticket.

checklist.step: Manage e-delivery consent records
actions: Verify each e-delivery customer holds a recorded, dated consent before any notice goes electronic-only.
Honour consent withdrawals within 5 business days by reverting the channel to post.
Sample 10 e-delivery sends monthly and confirm consent pre-dated the send.
Record the monthly sample result on the batch-control log.
checklist.done: e-delivery runs only on pre-dated consents with withdrawals honoured inside 5 days.

checklist.step: Report notice-timeliness KPIs to governance
actions: Publish the monthly scorecard from the BI/reporting platform: volumes by notice type, SLA attainment against the 99.5% line, breach causes, undeliverable counts and aging.
Review with the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager and agree corrective actions on any metric below the line.
Escalate two consecutive misses of the 99.5% line to the COO with a recovery plan.
File the scorecard in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a monthly scorecard is published, reviewed, actioned and filed, with escalation on repeat misses.

checklist.step: Retain notice evidence to the standard
actions: Apply the 10-year retention label to notice-log extracts, archived document copies, dispatch manifests and delivery confirmations in OpenText Document Mgmt.
Verify quarterly by retrieving five random notices end-to-end: log entry, archived copy, manifest, confirmation.
Fix any retrieval failure as a records incident with root cause.
Record the quarterly retrieval check.
checklist.done: retention is applied and quarterly retrieval checks prove end-to-end evidence for random notices.

checklist.step: Assess systemic failures for BMA self-report
actions: Review breach and missed-notice patterns quarterly against the Code's fair-treatment expectations.

Where a systemic failure materially affected policyholders (for example a class of lapse notices never sent), prepare a self-report to the BMA with the remediation plan, cleared by the General Counsel.
Record the assessment and decision each quarter, including 'no report required' conclusions with reasons.
Track any self-report commitments to completion.
checklist.done: a quarterly reportability assessment is recorded and any self-report is made with tracked commitments.

testing.step: Build the trigger-event population independently
actions: Extract all SLA-table trigger events for the quarter directly from the policy administration transaction data in the enterprise data warehouse — not from the notice log.
Total events by notice type as the independent population.
Reconcile the extract to the operations team's weekly reconciliations and investigate count differences.
testing.done: an independent trigger population is built from source data and reconciled to operations' counts.

testing.step: Match every trigger event to a notice-log entry
actions: Join the trigger population to the notice log on policy number, notice type and trigger date.
List every unmatched event as a missed notice — an automatic fail, no materiality screen.
Verify each miss was subsequently dispatched and impact-assessed.
testing.done: every trigger event matches a logged notice or is listed as a fail with its remediation status.

testing.step: Recompute the day count on the full quarter
actions: Recompute days-taken (dispatch date minus trigger date) for every logged notice and compare to each type's SLA day count from the approved table version in force at the trigger date.
Recompute the quarter's attainment rate and compare to the reported 99.5% scorecard figure.
A scorecard overstating attainment is itself an exception.
testing.done: independently recomputed attainment matches the scorecard and breaches are fully enumerated.

testing.step: Draw a sample and trace to delivery evidence
actions: Sample 25 notices (recorded seed) stratified across notice types, plus all breached notices up to 25.
For each, retrieve the archived document copy, dispatch manifest entry and mail-house or e-delivery confirmation from OpenText Document Mgmt.
Verify the archived copy is the approved template edition current at the send date (cross-check REG-054-C07 inventory).
Missing evidence at any link is an exception.
testing.done: sampled notices trace end-to-end to archived copy, manifest and delivery confirmation on the right edition.

testing.step: Verify trigger date integrity
actions: For 10 sampled notices, compare the stamped trigger date to the underlying transaction date in the Policy Administration Platform.
A trigger date later than the true event date shortens the customer's window and is a fail even if the SLA 'passed'.
Record the comparison table in the workpaper.
testing.done: stamped trigger dates equal true event dates for the sample.

testing.step: Test the failed-delivery workflow
actions: Sample 10 returned-mail or bounced-email cases from the quarter.
Verify address tracing, redispatch within 5 business days and the log update for each.
For undeliverables after two attempts, verify the diligence trail and policy flag exist.
A silently dropped notice is a fail with customer-impact referral.
testing.done: sampled delivery failures show timely redispatch or a documented diligence trail.

testing.step: Test e-delivery consent coverage
actions: Sample 10 electronic-only notices and verify a dated consent pre-dating each send.
Sample consent withdrawals in the quarter and verify channel reversion within 5 business days.
An electronic-only send without pre-dated consent is a fail.
testing.done: electronic-only sends all carry pre-dated consents and withdrawals reverted on time.

testing.step: Verify breach escalation and impact handling
actions: For every breach in the quarter, verify a tracker entry with cause, customer impact and same-day compliance notification.
Verify remedy-window extensions were applied where late notices shortened customer rights (for example late lapse warnings).
Verify the quarterly reportability assessment exists and covers the quarter's breach pattern.
testing.done: breaches show logged impact handling, remedy extensions where due, and a quarterly reportability assessment.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the notice id or event, requirement missed and customer impact.
Assign root cause (trigger config, batch, address quality, consent, evidence) and a named owner with a remediation date.
Refer systemic patterns to the Compliance Officer for the BMA self-report assessment.
Carry open items into next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: each exception is logged with root cause, owner, remediation date and systemic referral.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off and reporting
actions: State the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) against the 99.5% and zero-missed-notice thresholds with the recomputed figures.
Have the independent reviewer — outside Policy Administration operations — sign the workpaper.
Report quarterly results to the compliance committee and the COO.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-054-C08.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with recomputed metrics and a stated conclusion is filed and reported.
